title: Weight-only INT8 quant: CI golden-eval + calibration pipeline integration
creator: Emily Chen
description: Integrate a repeatable CI pipeline that runs weight-only INT8 quantization (GPTQ and AWQ variants) through a golden evaluation and calibration flow. The goal is to catch accuracy regressions early in PRs and on nightly runs for supported model families (e.g., Llama-2/13B, Mistral-7B, and internal reference variants). This ticket covers: orchestration of quant backends, synthetic and real calibration dataset generation, deterministic packing of state for reproducible downstream evaluation, and gating criteria for CI failures. The intent is not to replace full model evals but to provide a fast, high-signal regression gate for common failure modes introduced by changes to quant kernels, packing, or magic-number changes in GPTQ/AWQ code paths.
acceptance_criteria: CI job 'quant-int8-golden-eval' runs in under 45 minutes for 13B-family reference on our dedicated quant test pool
Calibration artifacts (per-layer scales, zero-points, activation histograms) are archived and linked to the job for failed runs
A golden-eval suite of ~120 prompts covering instruction, code, Q&A, and long-context continuation exists and is stable across runs
Regression thresholds are codified: LM loss delta <= 0.5% OR semantic-score delta <= 1.5% against golden baseline; exceeding either marks the run as failed
Both GPTQ and AWQ quant flows are exercised and produce comparable artifact metadata and regression labels
Failing jobs create an automated issue template with links to artifacts, diffs, model hashes, and the responsible PR
steps: Define a minimal golden prompt set and evaluation metrics with PM/AE input (pull sample set from existing evals and add targeted failure cases)
Implement a lightweight calibration generator that samples calibration batches from mini-datasets (mix of wiki, code, instruction) and emits per-layer statistics
Abstract the quant backend interface in CI so GPTQ and AWQ runs share orchestration, artifact naming, and caching rules
Add deterministic seed paths for packing and quantization steps to make runs reproducible across machines
Wire CI job to store artifacts in S3 with consistent naming: quant-int8/{model}/{backend}/{timestamp}/{git_sha}
Implement regression gating logic in the CI workflow; add a try-fix step that triggers a targeted re-run with increased numerical tolerance for flaky metrics
Publish results to the runtime dashboard and add a per-job link to the Linear ticket when failures occur
regression_thresholds: LM-loss-delta<=0.5% || semantic-score-delta<=1.5% ; max-acceptable-generation-drop=2 tokens avg ; flakiness-tolerance=2 of 3 reruns
testing_environments: quant-test-pool (p4d), quant-ci-small (g5), local dev with cpu fallback
notes: We intentionally keep the golden-eval small so it can run on PRs; nightly runs expand to full evals. Use floating calibration seed to surface edge cases in activation ranges. Documented failure modes: rounding drift in AWQ packing, histogram outliers caused by layout change, and KV cache noise affecting long-context continuations.
